newsitem.title: USA: Excel sees Q4 between $0.27 and $0.30/shr.
newsitem.headline: Excel sees Q4 between $0.27 and $0.30/shr.

text.p: EXCEL Communications Inc said on Monday it expected to earn between $0.27 and $0.30 per share in the fourth quarter, due to operational constraints related to network capacity.
The company said while these results were below analyst projections, it expected its 1997 results to be in line with analysts' estimates.
The First Call earnings estimate for the fourth quarter was $0.43 per share and the 1997 estimate was $2.07 per share.

"The magnitude of migrating more than four million subscribers across approximately 900 Local Exchange Carriers (LECs) to three new networks created some disruption in the flow of data between the LECs, the underlying carriers, and EXCEL," John McLaine, executive vice president and chief financial officer, said.
These difficulties continued to bear on subscriber attrition and call volume in the fourth quarter, he said.

Excel previously said it had identified operational difficulties late in the second quarter, due to the failure of its long distance carrier to add network capacity needed to handle its subscriber base growth and long distance traffic.

The company said the blockage experienced in several states as a result of the network capacity problems caused a slowdown in marketing activities, a loss of subscribers, and reduced calling activity during the third quarter.
"By the end of the third quarter, we saw our attrition rate reach above-normal levels and our subscriber calling activity decline because of the network capacity issues," McLaine said.
Excel said it expected communications revenue of $40 million and a reduction in earnings per share of about $0.17 for the fourth quarter due to these problems.
But McLaine said the company believed these were largely behind it.
EXCEL said planned to begin installing its own switches in 1997. This would further protect EXCEL from the capacity problems it encountered with its former carrier, it said.
"With the completion of our subscriber migration to the networks of IXC, MCI, and WorldCom, we do not expect to encounter network capacity problems in the foreseeable future," McLaine said.
